claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for. Let me ask you some key questions:

**First, what is the age of the child you're wanting to claim Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- Their name
- Their date of birth (or current age)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I'm asking about my child Alex. He's 13 years old. I want to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a child named **Alex who is 13 years old**. That's helpful to know.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, he falls into the first category for Child Benefit eligibility. Now I need to check a few more things to determine if you can claim for him.

Let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex working full-time (16 hours or more per week)?**

This is important because even though he's under 16, there are rules about full-time work that could affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 13, so he's still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's good to know. Since Alex is 13, under 16, and not working full-time, he meets the basic child requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

Now I need to check some other important criteria that apply to you as the claimant. Let me navigate to the next set of checks:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 13 and not working at all, this check is straightforward for him. He's definitely not working 24 hours or more per week, so he passes this requirement.

Let me continue checking the other eligibility criteria:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (as an individual claimant, not as a dependent)
- Income Support
- Jobseeker's Allowance

Please let me know if Alex is receiving any of these benefits.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits himself. He's just a kid - I'm the one who handles all that sort of thing.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfect! Since Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own right, he passes this check too.

Let me continue with the next requirement:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 13 and still in school, I'd expect the answer is no, but I want to check to be thorough. Please let me know if he is in any apprenticeship program.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's only 13 and still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now I need to check some criteria about you as the claimant. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status as the claimant. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

**Which of the following best describes your situation?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and I'd need to ask follow-up questions about your work/study situation)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries
5. **Something else?**

Please let me know which applies to you, or if you're not sure about any of these categories.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that! Since you're living abroad, I need to ask a few more questions to see if you still qualify for Child Benefit.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **What is your employment or status abroad?** For example:
   - Are you working abroad?
   - Are you a Crown servant (working for the UK government/civil service)?
   - Are you studying?
   - Are you in a different situation?

2. **Do you have any UK visa or immigration status?** For example:
   - Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Are you a British citizen?
   - Something else?

These details will help me determine if living abroad affects your eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not a Crown servant - I'm just living abroad for personal reasons. I am a British citizen, but I don't currently live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. As a British citizen living abroad, I need to understand your situation a bit better to see if you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**A few more questions:**

1. **Do you still have a permanent home or ties in the UK?** For example:
   - Do you own or rent a property in the UK?
   - Do you have family in the UK?
   - Do you plan to return to the UK?

2. **Are you working abroad, or what is your current situation regarding employment/income?**

3. **Which country are you currently living in?**

The reason I'm asking is that even though you're a British citizen, Child Benefit eligibility for people living abroad can depend on factors like whether you're still considered to "normally live" in the UK or whether you meet other specific criteria. Being a British citizen living abroad doesn't automatically qualify you, but your specific circumstances matter.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad indefinitely - I don't have a permanent home in the UK anymore. I'm just working a regular job where I am now. I'm not planning to return to the UK in the near future.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you giving me that context. Based on what you've described - you're living abroad indefinitely, don't have a permanent home in the UK anymore, and aren't planning to return soon - this suggests you would not normally be considered as "normally living in the UK," which is the primary requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

However, before I make a final determination, let me check if there are any other paths that might apply to your situation. Let me ask one more thing:

**Do you have or are you eligible for any of the following immigration statuses:**
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?

Or are you simply a British citizen living and working abroad with no other special immigration status?

If you're just a British citizen with no EU Settlement Scheme status, then unfortunately this would make you ineligible for Child Benefit, as you would not meet the residency requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm just a British citizen - no special EU Settlement Scheme status or anything like that. I'm simply living and working abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on your situation, I'm afraid I need to give you the outcome of the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Outcome

**Result: INELIGIBLE ❌**

---

### Summary

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex, even though Alex himself would meet all the requirements to be a qualifying child.

### Why You're Ineligible

**Reason:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

To claim Child Benefit, you must normally live in the UK. As a British citizen living abroad indefinitely without a permanent home in the UK and with no plans to return, you do not meet this fundamental requirement.

### What This Means

- While Alex (age 13) meets all the child-specific eligibility criteria (not working full-time, not receiving benefits, not in an apprenticeship), **the claimant's residency status is the barrier**
- Simply being a British citizen is not enough - you must also normally reside in the UK
- Special EU Settlement Scheme status could have provided alternative paths to eligibility, but you don't have that

### Possible Next Steps

If your circumstances change - for example:
- If you return to the UK and establish normal UK residency
- If you acquire settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

...you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit in the future.

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I'm sorry I couldn't provide a positive outcome in this case. If you have any other questions or if your situation changes, please feel free to ask!
